name: LEXICON
expansion: Lexical Encoding of eXperiment Information as Checked Observable tokeNs

intro.problem: Detector events are treated as vectors of continuous features, and the language-model tools that learn structure from co-occurrence have not been tested on whether events carry a grammar of their own.
intro.value: If they do, a token model trained only on background could score how typical an event is, giving a new axis for data-driven background estimation and a new kind of input for classifiers.
intro.approach: We quantize each feature into a small number of levels so an event becomes a set of tokens, screen tokenizations against raw-value controls, and train background-only density models whose surprise score is tested against independence baselines.
intro.goals: The goal is a vetted tokenization, a background token model with a usable surprise score, and a clear verdict on whether tokens add information beyond the raw features, followed by supervised and embedding routes.

questions: Does co-occurrence among binned detector features carry signal-versus-background information beyond the raw values?
Can a background-only token model supply a usable axis for a data-driven background estimate?
Are per-event embeddings more useful than per-token ones?

timeline.label: Tokenization line kicked off under HELIX: design work and first test scripts
Phase 1: first discretization checks run across all four detector lanes
Tokenization plan deck drafted: token units, edge schemes and test paths
Sub-project renamed LEXICON, under the HELIX umbrella
First screening rules fixed: information gate, occupancy floor, path rules
Route A (unsupervised background-only token model) first run reviewed
Route B (supervised on tokens) and Route C (tokens into the networks)
